item.text: {"text":"Published gBCE uses L = [−β log σ(s⁺) − Σⱼ log(1−σ(sⱼ⁻))]/(k+1), where k is sampled negatives per positive, α=k/(|I|−1), and |I| counts actual catalog items. The calibration mapping is β=α[t(1−1/α)+1/α]=1−t+αt. Thus t=0 gives β=1 (ordinary BCE); t=1 gives β=α (full calibration under the paper’s assumptions). Increasing t decreases β and reduces overconfidence. The proposed β=α+t(1−α) reverses these endpoints and does not reproduce the published t convention. [Official paper](https://eprints.gla.ac.uk/301348/3/301348.pdf)\n\nThe correct positive term is −log(σ(s)ᵝ)=β·softplus(−s). The complement-power expression −log(1−(1−σ(s))ᵝ) is a different objective, except at β=1. A direct stable implementation per target is `(beta * F.softplus(-pos) + F.softplus(neg).sum(-1)) / (k + 1)`, averaged over valid targets. The official PyTorch implementation instead transforms positive logits to γ(s)=−log(σ(s)^(−β)−1), applies ordinary BCE, averages across all k+1 candidates, then averages valid positions. Summing negative losses preserves the published relative weighting; replacing that sum with a negative mean while leaving the positive term unchanged changes the objective. Applying this loss to BERT4Rec should retain masked-target training and its bidirectional backbone. [Official training code](https://github.com/asash/gSASRec-pytorch/blob/main/train_gsasrec.py)"}
